claim: Heron is a Python-based platform for constructing and running experimental and data analysis pipelines.
source: To address this, we present Heron, a Python-based platform for constructing and running experimental and data analysis pipelines.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract of the manuscript.

claim: Heron allows researchers to design experiments according to their own mental schemata, represented as a Knowledge Graph.
source: Heron allows researchers to design experiments according to their own mental schemata, represented as a Knowledge Graph – a structure that mirrors the logical flow of an experiment.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract describing Heron's design philosophy.

claim: Heron supports the integration of software and hardware combinations that are otherwise too complex or costly.
source: Heron supports the integration of software and hardware combinations that are otherwise too complex or costly, making it especially useful in experimental sciences with a large number of interconnected components such as robotics, neuroscience, behavioural sciences, physics, chemistry, and environmental sciences.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract as a key capability of Heron.

claim: Heron assumes intermediate Python proficiency from its users.
source: It assumes intermediate Python proficiency and offers a clean, modular code base that encourages documentation and reuse.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract regarding user requirements.

claim: The translation from mental schema to running code base makes design iteration efforts practically impossible due to prohibitively large iteration time.
source: Finally, the complexity of the translation from mental schema to running code base makes design iteration efforts practically impossible. The prohibitively large iteration time, on the one hand, and the inter-dependency of engineering decisions throughout the implementation cycle, on the other hand, make updates of the experimental flow extremely cumbersome.
evidence: Stated as a problem that Heron aims to address in the introduction.

claim: Object-oriented programming has been an effort to replace low-level concepts with bundles of higher-level ones that are easier to cognise.
source: Concepts like object-oriented programming (Kindler and Krivy, 2011) or actor-based programming (Agha, 1986) for example, have been nothing else but an effort to take away the low-level concepts that one needs to ultimately manipulate and replace them with bundles of higher-level ones, easier to cognise with.
evidence: Stated with citations to support the historical context of programming paradigms.

claim: Heron creates experimental pipelines that visually and structurally bear a very significant resemblance to the original mental schema of the experimental pipeline.
source: The primary one is that it creates experimental pipelines that visually and structurally bear a very significant resemblance to the original mental schema of the experimental pipeline.
evidence: Directly stated as Heron's primary distinguishing feature.

claim: Heron targets experimenters without expertise in arcane subjects like networking, hardware connectivity, or low-level software–hardware interactions.
source: A second distinguishing feature of Heron is that it targets the experimenter without expertise in arcane subjects like networking, hardware connectivity, or low-level software–hardware interactions.
evidence: Directly stated as a distinguishing feature of Heron.

claim: A mental schema is a psychological concept that defines the way humans cognise.
source: A mental schema is a psychological concept (Bartlett and Burt, 1933, Williams, 2019) that is meant to define the way humans cognise.
evidence: Stated with citations to psychological literature.

claim: A Knowledge Graph is a mathematical structure designed to capture unstructured human knowledge in a machine-implementable way.
source: A KG (Fensel et al., 2020) is a mathematical structure designed to capture the unstructured human knowledge on a subject (i.e. the mental schemata of different individuals relating to the same knowledge corpus) in such a way that a machine could use it to test propositions against the knowledge and also create novel propositions that a human with the knowledge would find to be true.
evidence: Stated with citation to define Knowledge Graphs.

claim: Heron implements an experiment in the form of a Knowledge Graph at two separate levels: graphical and code.
source: Heron implements an experiment in the form of a KG and does so at two separate levels. One is the graphical level, where a series of Nodes and their in-between links (Edges) are defined. The second is the code that defines each Node's functionality.
evidence: Stated in text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Heron's code base is implemented in Python.
source: Heron's code base is implemented in Python.
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript.

claim: Python was chosen for Heron to keep the code simple while being able to interact with diverse hardware drivers and software analysis libraries.
source: This choice was informed by the need to keep the code simple to implement while at the same time being able to interact with a very diverse list of hardware drivers and software analysis libraries (see Design benefits section).
evidence: Stated as the rationale for choosing Python.

claim: Heron allows users to implement Nodes in languages other than Python.
source: Yet the language that Heron itself is implemented in (Python) does not enforce the language new Nodes can be implemented in by Heron users.
evidence: Directly stated as a capability of Heron.

claim: MATLAB Simulink and LabVIEW are frameworks where experiments can be designed as computational graphs using predefined elements.
source: MATLAB Simulink (Acklam, 2003) and LabVIEW (Bitter and Nawrocki, 2006) are two of the more well-known frameworks where experiments can be designed as computational graphs using predefined elements (i.e. nodes provided by the developers of these systems).
evidence: Stated with citations as background on computational graph frameworks.

claim: Bonsai is a framework originally designed to ease the implementation of neuroscience and behavioural science experiments.
source: Bonsai (Lopes et al., 2015) is a new entry to this field originally designed to ease the implementation of neuroscience and behavioural science experiments.
evidence: Stated with citation as background on similar tools.

claim: EPypes is a Python-based software framework for developing vision algorithms in a form of computational graphs.
source: EPypes is (according to the developers' own description) a 'Python-based software framework for developing vision algorithms in a form of computational graphs and their integration with distributed systems based on publish-subscribe communication'.
evidence: Stated as a description of EPypes from its developers.

claim: ROS implements a peer-to-peer network of processes that are loosely coupled using ROS communication infrastructure.
source: The exact same idea is utilised by ROS where (in their own words again) 'The ROS runtime 'graph' is a peer-to-peer network of processes (potentially distributed across machines) that are loosely coupled using the ROS communication infrastructure. ROS implements several different styles of communication, including synchronous RPC-style communication over services, asynchronous streaming of data over topics, and storage of data on a Parameter Server'.
evidence: Stated as a description from ROS documentation.

claim: Hybrid programming combining visual and textual programming was found to allow for better retention of computer software university students.
source: This hybrid approach was found to allow for a better retention of computer software university students, when comparing only textual or only visual styles in the learning of programming (Noone and Mooney, 2018), showing that it better suits beginner level programmers (a category into which a large percentage of experimentalists fall in).
evidence: Stated with citation to educational research.

claim: pyControl, Bpod, and Autopilot are frameworks that specifically target behavioural sciences fields.
source: Other frameworks that specifically target the same fields are pyControl (Akam et al., 2022), Bpod (Sanworks LLC, USA) (building on the central design concept of B-control; Brody, 2007), and Autopilot (Saunders and Wehr, 2019).
evidence: Stated with citations as background on similar tools.

claim: Heron's Knowledge Graph immediately offers a succinct overview of the experimental workflow and dynamics, acting as primary documentation.
source: The KG of Heron immediately offers a succinct overview of the experimental workflow and the dynamics it implements, thus acting also as the primary documentation of the experiment.
evidence: Stated as a design benefit of Heron.

claim: In Heron, each Node runs its own process separate from all the programs of the other Nodes.
source: In Heron, each Node runs its own process (practically its own little program, separate from all the programs of the other Nodes).
evidence: Directly stated as a technical characteristic of Heron.

claim: Heron's multi-process approach allows running different Nodes on different machines.
source: This multi-process approach offers an important competence; running different Nodes on different machines (albeit by taking a hit on system resources vs a multi-threaded approach).
evidence: Stated as a capability enabled by the multi-process architecture.

claim: Heron has been tested to be operational under Windows 10 and 11, Linux PC Ubuntu 20.04.6, MacOS, and Raspberry Pi 4.
source: Heron itself (the GUI and underlying communication functionality) has been tested to be operational under Windows (10 and 11, both ×64), Linux PC (Ubuntu 20.04.6, ×64) MacOS, and Raspberry Pi 4 (Debian GNU/Linux 12 -bookworm-, aarch64).
evidence: Directly stated as tested configurations.

claim: Python's extensive community has contributed to an open source ecosystem of libraries for practically any computation imaginable.
source: Apart from this, batteries included, Python's approach to problems, the main advantage for experiment implementation is Python's extensive community of developers that have contributed to the open source ecosystem of Python libraries for practically any computation imaginable.
evidence: Stated as an advantage of using Python.

claim: 0MQ is a versatile and easy to use library for passing messages across different processes running on different machines.
source: For the cases where a user with deeper knowledge of software engineering has a specific need to use other languages, Heron offers one last benefit arising from the use of its message passing library, 0MQ (Hintjens, 2013). 0MQ is a versatile and easy to use library for passing messages across different processes running on different machines.
evidence: Stated with citation describing 0MQ.

claim: Heron defines three different types of Nodes: Sources, Transforms, and Sinks.
source: Heron defines three different types of Nodes, each implementing a different basic functionality of message passing. Those are the Sources, the Transforms and the Sinks (see the orange, green, and purple Nodes, respectively, in the example KG of Figure 1B).
evidence: Stated in text and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Source Nodes generate data and can only transmit data through the Nodes' outputs.
source: The Sources are Nodes that generate data (either computationally or by reading them from a device) and thus can only transmit data through the Nodes' outputs.
evidence: Directly stated as a definition of Source Nodes.

claim: Transform Nodes can both receive and transmit data through both input and output points and are meant to allow data manipulation.
source: The Transform Nodes can both receive and transmit data through both input and output points and are meant to allow data manipulation.
evidence: Directly stated as a definition of Transform Nodes.

claim: Sink Nodes can only receive data and only feature input points.
source: Finally, the Sink Nodes can only receive data and only feature input points.
evidence: Directly stated as a definition of Sink Nodes.

claim: Heron's processes do not allow each other to take control of each other and change each other's state in an actor-based model.
source: Heron's processes do not allow each other to take control of each other and change each other's state. Each process has full control of its state and will only allow another process to influence it through the passing of messages. This is known as the actor-based model.
evidence: Directly stated as Heron's architectural approach.

claim: When a Graph is not running, Heron acts as a Graph designer offering a GUI where users can create and delete Nodes, connect them with Links and assign values to their parameters.
source: When a Graph (short for KG) is not running, Heron acts as a Graph designer, offering a GUI where a user can create and delete Nodes, connect them with Links and assign values to their parameters.
evidence: Directly stated as Heron's dual role.

claim: When a Knowledge Graph is running, Heron assumes the role of a director in an actor-based model and can compute and run a GUI for the experiment.
source: When, on the other hand, a KG is running, the Heron process stops being a Graph design application and assumes the role of a director in an actor-based model (Agha, 1986). It can then concurrently compute and run a GUI for the experiment where the user can update the parameters of the different Nodes on the fly (as an experimental Control Panel).
evidence: Stated with citation describing Heron's runtime behavior.

claim: A running Heron experiment is constituted by (Number of Nodes) × 2 + 4 processes.
source: That means a running experiment is constituted by (Number of Nodes) × 2 + 4 processes (see Figure 2).
evidence: Stated in text and illustrated in Figure 2.

claim: Each Node in Heron is represented by two processes called the com and worker process.
source: As mentioned above, each Node is represented by two processes. In the code, those are called the com and worker process.
evidence: Directly stated as Heron's architecture.

claim: The worker process runs the Node's script defined by the user.
source: The worker process is the one that runs the Node's script defined by the user.
evidence: Directly stated as the function of the worker process.

claim: The com process is responsible for grabbing messages from other Nodes, passing them to the worker process, receiving messages from the worker process, and passing those messages to other Nodes.
source: The com process is responsible for (1) grabbing messages that come out of other Nodes and are meant to reach the Node (as defined by a Link between two Nodes in the Node Editor), (2) passing those messages to the worker process, (3) receiving any messages the worker process has to pass to other Nodes, and (4) passing those messages to the com processes of all the Nodes that should receive them.
evidence: Directly stated as the function of the com process.

claim: Heron allows any of the Nodes in a Graph to be initiated and executed in machines different from the one running the main Heron process.
source: As mentioned above, Heron allows any of the Nodes in a Graph to be initiated and executed in machines different to the one running the main Heron process.
evidence: Directly stated as a capability of Heron.

claim: Heron's code is separated into three main folders: Communications, GUI, and Operations.
source: Heron's code is separated into three main folders, each pertaining to one of the three aspects of its basic functionality (see Appendix 1—figure 1 for all of Heron's folder structures). The Communications folder includes scripts that deal with the low-level communication between all Nodes that make up a running Graph (experiment). The GUI folder holds scripts that deal with Heron's GUI. The Operations folder keeps all the code that defines all the Nodes that Heron recognises and can use to create a Graph with.
evidence: Directly stated as the code organization structure.

claim: In Heron all messages are either numpy arrays or Python dictionaries.
source: This is required because in Heron all messages are either numpy arrays or Python dictionaries.
evidence: Directly stated as a technical requirement.

claim: The worker functions of Source and Transform Nodes will always return either a list of numpy arrays or a list of dictionaries.
source: That means that the worker functions of the worker scripts of the Source and Transform Nodes will always return either a list of numpy arrays or a list of dictionaries.
evidence: Directly stated as a technical requirement for Node implementation.

claim: Heron is designed to have no message buffering, thus automatically dropping any messages that come into a Node's inputs while the Node's worker function is still running.
source: Both the Transform and the Sink Nodes will stop accepting messages until their worker functions have returned, and Heron is designed to have no message buffering, thus automatically dropping any messages that come into a Node's inputs while the Node's worker function is still running.
evidence: Directly stated as a design characteristic of Heron.

claim: Heron comes pre-packaged with a small set of Nodes that have generic enough usage that most users would find useful.
source: Heron comes pre-packaged with a small set of Nodes that have a generic enough usage that most users would find useful.
evidence: Directly stated as what comes with Heron.

claim: Heron is designed to easily access repos that have been developed following a specific file structure to represent a set of Heron Nodes.
source: Heron is designed to easily access repos that have been developed following a specific file structure to represent a set of Heron Nodes and integrate them into its GUI and workflow without the user needing to do anything else other than create/download the repository and point Heron to it.
evidence: Directly stated as a capability for adding new Nodes.

claim: Heron's GUI allows easy definition of the local access network of machines that will run Nodes forming a single pipeline.
source: Heron's GUI allows an easy definition of the local access network (LAN) of machines that will run Nodes forming a single pipeline.
evidence: Directly stated as a GUI capability.

claim: Heron allows many-to-many connectivity, meaning a Node's output can connect to any number of inputs and an input can receive any number of outputs.
source: Heron allows many-to-many connectivity, meaning a Node's output can connect to any number of inputs and an input can receive any number of outputs.
evidence: Directly stated as a connectivity feature.

claim: Heron provides a set of templates that offer a scaffold on top of which users can build their own code.
source: To facilitate this, Heron provides a series of tools. Firstly, there is a set of templates that offer a scaffold on top of which a user can build their own code.
evidence: Directly stated as a tool for Node development.

claim: Heron provides a GUI-based system for generating new Nodes.
source: On top of Node templates, Heron provides a GUI-based system for generating new Nodes.
evidence: Directly stated as a tool for Node development.

claim: A public GitHub organisation called Heron-Repositories is hosting both the main Heron Git repository and all other Git repositories of Nodes.
source: Currently, a public GitHub organisation called (rather unimaginatively) Heron-Repositories is hosting both the main Heron Git repository and all other Git repositories of Nodes developed to cover the developers' experimental needs.
evidence: Directly stated as the location of Heron repositories.

claim: The Probabilistic Reversal Learning experiment's Knowledge Graph is made up of four Nodes.
source: As seen in Figure 3, this experimental pipeline is made up of four Nodes.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 3.

claim: The Fetching experiment requires monitoring a rodent as it tries to fetch a cotton bud from a random point in a large arena and drop it into a shallow pot.
source: The experiment itself requires the monitoring of a rodent as it tries to fetch a cotton bud from a random point in a large arena and drop it into a shallow pot under a hole at one of its corners.
evidence: Directly stated as the experimental design.

claim: The Fetching experiment uses a Grasshopper3 USB 3.0 colour camera that records at 120 frames per second with HD resolution.
source: The hardware setup has a Grasshopper3 USB 3.0 colour camera (GS3-U3-23S6C-C, FLIR) which records the whole of the arena from the top at 120 frames per second with HD resolution, while 4 smaller, black and white, 30 frames per second cameras (OV9281, ArduCam) are used to capture the animal from three different angles and to also monitor the target pot from underneath (since its base is transparent plastic) using the fourth camera.
evidence: Directly stated as part of the hardware setup.

claim: The Grasshopper camera at the time of the experiment's development could run only on Python 3.8.
source: The Grasshopper camera at the time of the experiment's development could run only on Python 3.8.
evidence: Directly stated as a hardware constraint.

claim: The angle detection of the cotton bud is done using Meta's Detectron 2, a deep learning algorithm.
source: The angle detection of the cotton bud when it is in the pot is done using Meta's Detectron 2 (Wu et al., 2019), a deep learning algorithm which we trained with a few hundred samples to detect the cotton bud's edges when in the pot using as an input the part of the OV9281 camera frames that come from the camera underneath the pot.
evidence: Stated with citation describing the algorithm used.

claim: Detectron 2 requires an Intel or AMD CPU-based computer running Linux.
source: Detectron 2 requires an Intel or AMD CPU-based computer running Linux.
evidence: Directly stated as a requirement for the algorithm.

claim: The Fetching experiment pipeline utilizes two physically separate machines, three operating systems and four different Python environments.
source: To summarise, the pipeline (which can be seen in Figure 4) when run, is utilising two physically separate machines, three operating systems (one Windows 11 and two Linux, one on a virtual machine) and four different Python environments.
evidence: Stated in text and illustrated in Figure 4.

claim: The rats playing computer games experiment teaches a rat to rotate a line on a screen using left and right lever presses to hit a target line and avoid a trap line.
source: The rats playing computer games experiment teaches a rat to rotate a line on a screen using a left and a right lever press to hit a target line and avoid a trap line.
evidence: Directly stated as the experimental design.

claim: In the Unity game engine, a simple 2D game was made using C# code that covered all possible visual stimuli needed for the rats playing computer games experiment.
source: In the Unity game engine (Unity Technologies, US) we made a simple 2D game using C# code, that covered all the possible visual stimuli we needed to show to the animals at any stage (see Figure 5D for a snapshot of the Unity development environment).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The Unity-generated executable used NetMQ, one of many C# 0MQ bindings, to receive commands through a 0MQ SUB socket.
source: Instead of using the standard game inputs (e.g. keyboard or game controller) to control what and when was played on the screen, we used a string of commands that was received by the game executable through a 0MQ SUB socket (using NetMQ, one of many C# 0MQ bindings).
evidence: Directly stated as the implementation approach.

claim: The rats playing computer games experiment with a 15 node Graph was conducted on a Windows 10 × 64 machine with an 8 core i7-7700K CPU clocking at 4.20 GHz.
source: The experiment was conducted on a Windows 10 × 64 machine with an 8 core i7-7700K CPU clocking at 4.20 GHz.
evidence: Directly stated as the hardware configuration.

claim: When the rats playing computer games experiment was running, the CPU load hit 100% with the Unity game requiring around 24% and the remaining 45–55% used by the Graph's 32 processes.
source: With the above experiment running, the CPU load hit 100% with the Unity game requiring around 24% and the remaining 45–55% used by the Graph's 32 processes (one process was running on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano machine).
evidence: Directly stated as measured CPU usage.

claim: Setting 10 of the 15 worker processes to specific CPUs dropped the total CPU load to 80% in the rats playing computer games experiment.
source: Rerunning the above Graph while setting 10 of the 15 worker processes to specific CPUs and allowing the system to optimise the load for only 5 of them (the Spinnaker Camera, Save FFMPEG Video, Arducam Quadrascopic Camera, Save Array To Binary, and TL Taks2 Screens Unity) dropped the total CPU load to 80%, again with the Unity game consuming around 24% while all Graph python processes consuming around 25%.
evidence: Directly stated as measured CPU usage with optimization.

claim: Heron offers a set of tools to allow users to time-align every single packet of data generated and saved by any Node to any other packet irrespective of whether the packets were generated by Nodes on the same or separate machines.
source: Heron offers a set of tools to allow users to time-align every single packet of data generated and saved by any Node to any other packet irrespective of whether the packets were generated by Nodes on the same or separate machines.
evidence: Directly stated as a capability of Heron.

claim: A 120-fps projector was used as the base clock in the rats playing computer games experiment synchronization setup.
source: We use a 120-fps projector (whose output is controlled by the Node TL Projector Output##0) to act as our base clock.
evidence: Stated in text and illustrated in Figure 5C.

claim: The Spinnaker camera generated a total of 216300 frames, and the final video had a total of 216,244 frames, a drop of 56 frames over the two Nodes, that is 0.02%.
source: In the shown example, the camera generated a total of 216300 frames, and the final video had a total of 216,244 frames, a drop of 56 frames dropped over the two Nodes, that is a 0.02%.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5C showing the synchronization example.

claim: Heron allows the Worker process of any Node to update its parameters as they are changed by the experimenter through the GUI while the Graph is running.
source: Heron allowed us to operate in this 'experimenter in the loop' fashion because it allows the Worker process of any Node to update its parameters as they are changed by the experimenter through the GUI while the Graph is running.
evidence: Directly stated as a capability for on-the-fly control.

claim: All experiments were performed in accordance with the UK Home Office regulations Animal (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986 and the Animal Welfare and Ethical Review Body (AWERB).
source: All experiments were performed in accordance with the UK Home Office regulations Animal (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986 and the Animal Welfare and Ethical Review Body (AWERB).
evidence: Directly stated as ethical approval.

claim: For the Fetching and Computer Games experiments, subjects were adult male Lister Hooded rats from Charles River.
source: For the Fetching and Computer Games experiments, subjects were adult male Lister Hooded rats (Charles River), which were kept on a reversed 12-hr light–dark cycle.
evidence: Directly stated as animal details.

claim: A total of 10 rats were used in the Fetching and Computer Games behavioural experiments.
source: A total of 10 were used in the behavioural experiments.
evidence: Directly stated as the number of subjects.

claim: Mouse experiments for the Probabilistic Reversal Learning experiment were conducted using male WT C57/BL6 mice aged 6–8 weeks at the start of experiments.
source: Mouse experiments for the Probabilistic Reversal Learning experiment were conducted using male WT C57/BL6 (Charles River), aged at 6–8 weeks at the start of experiments.
evidence: Directly stated as animal details.

claim: A total of four mice were used in the Probabilistic Reversal Learning experiment.
source: A total of four mice were used.
evidence: Directly stated as the number of subjects.

claim: Heron's implementation of an experiment becomes the easiest way for non-developers to acquaint themselves with the experiment and its logic.
source: The first experimental example is provided here to showcase how Heron's implementation of an experiment becomes the easiest way for non-developers to acquaint themselves with the experiment and its logic.
evidence: Stated as the purpose of the Probabilistic Reversal Learning example.

claim: Heron is an open source software with an MIT license.
source: In order to address this discrepancy between the mental schemata and implementation outcomes in experimental construction, we developed Heron, an open source software (MIT license) platform for the construction of data flow pipelines (e.g. experiments, data analysis, robotics, etc.).
evidence: Directly stated in the introduction.

claim: Heron's learning curve, starting from a basic capability in Python, is measured in the few hours of trying to create a couple of new Nodes.
source: We are arguing here that Heron's learning curve, starting from a basic capability in Python, is measured in the few hours of trying to create a couple of new Nodes and joining those together in order to create some toy experiment.
evidence: Stated as an assessment of Heron's ease of use.

claim: Heron has been conceptualised to grow into a community project.
source: Heron has been conceptualised to grow into a community project.
evidence: Directly stated as the vision for Heron.

claim: Both Heron and the repositories holding extra Heron Nodes are open source under an MIT licence.
source: Both itself and the repositories holding extra Heron Nodes are open source under an MIT licence.
evidence: Directly stated regarding licensing.

claim: The separation of repositories that hold the main Heron code and the individual Nodes' code bases allows for the growth of a Node ecosystem.
source: The separation of repositories that hold the main Heron code and the individual Nodes' code bases allows for the growth of a Node ecosystem where users will be able to share their development using standard repository-based tools.
evidence: Stated as a design benefit for community development.

claim: Heron's name is a tribute to Hero of Alexandria, one of the first known creators of automata.
source: Heron's name is a tribute to one of the first known creators of automata, Hero of Alexandria.
evidence: Directly stated as the origin of the name.

claim: Using multiple processes rather than multiple threads incurs a hit in the total CPU load Heron will require to execute a Graph.
source: Using multiple processes rather than multiple threads does incur a hit in the total CPU load Heron will require in order to execute a Graph.
evidence: Directly stated as a trade-off of the multi-process approach.

claim: Heron has a feature which allows the user to force the operating system to keep a worker process running on a specific CPU core.
source: Heron has a feature which allows the user to force the operating system to keep a worker process running on a specific CPU core.
evidence: Directly stated as a feature for CPU optimization.

claim: Heron's ability to utilise multiple machines in a single Graph means that processes requiring exceptional CPU, memory and/or GPU loads can be offloaded to machines other than the one running the Heron GUI.
source: Also, Heron's ability to utilise multiple machines in a single Graph means that processes requiring exceptional CPU, memory and/or GPU loads can be offloaded to machines other than the one running the Heron GUI.
evidence: Stated as a capability for handling computational demands.

claim: Multiple processes running over different machines can become extremely difficult to synchronise, especially to the tight requirements of a scientific experiment.
source: Multiple processes, running over different machines, can become extremely difficult to synchronise, especially to the tight requirements of a scientific experiment.
evidence: Stated as a challenge that Heron addresses.

claim: A Substate dataframe is Heron's way to allow the designer of a Node to save information to a pandas dataframe every time the Worker process runs a pass through its loop.
source: A Substate dataframe is Heron's way to allow the designer of a Node to save information (to a pandas dataframe) every time the Worker process runs a pass through its loop.
evidence: Directly stated as a feature for data logging.

claim: A Com processes log file records the id of any packet that arrives from an upstream Node and the id of that packet as given by the current Node.
source: A Com processes log file (optionally set for any Node by filling in the log file's path to the Node's secondary window appropriate entry) records the id of any packet that arrives from an upstream Node as given by that Node and the id of that packet as given by the current Node.
evidence: Directly stated as a feature for tracking data packets.

claim: Heron does not offer any capability to buffer packets.
source: As mentioned before, Heron does not offer any capability to buffer packets, so if the FFMPEG Node is too late to save any frame, then the next one gets lost.
evidence: Directly stated as a design characteristic.

claim: The rats playing computer games experiment is a very challenging behaviour for a rat and needs several stages of shaping to teach it to the animals.
source: This is a very challenging behaviour for a rat, and the experiment needs several stages of shaping to teach it to the animals.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of the experimental task.

claim: The statemachine Python library allows the definition of a state machine and its individual states with easily attachable callbacks at state transitions.
source: Here, we used statemachine (Macedo, 2025), a Python library that allows the definition of a state machine and its individual states with easily attachable callbacks at state transitions.
evidence: Stated with citation describing the library used.

claim: Heron offers users a comfortable starting point to implement their own Nodes in Python while allowing expert users to utilise lower-level languages.
source: Heron offers users a comfortable starting point to implement their own Nodes (in Python), while allowing for expert users to utilise lower-level languages that offer other advantages like faster run times and lower-level control of a machine's components (e.g. CPUs, GPUs, RAM, etc.).
evidence: Directly stated as a design feature.

claim: Heron poses very few (if any) limitations in what types of behaviour can be implemented in any Node.
source: Heron poses very few (if any) limitations in what types of behaviour can be implemented in any Node.
evidence: Stated as a design characteristic.

claim: Heron does not offer a long list of predefined Nodes which would make very strong assumptions about the structure of the experiment's mental schema.
source: In this way, Heron does not offer a long list of predefined Nodes which would make very strong assumptions about the structure of the experiment's mental schema.
evidence: Stated as a distinguishing design choice.

claim: Heron offers the tools for designing and implementing one's own Nodes in a case-by-case approach at a level of abstraction required at any time.
source: Instead, it offers the tools for designing and implementing one's own Nodes in a case-by-case approach at a level of abstraction required at any time.
evidence: Stated as Heron's approach to Node design.

claim: 0MQ includes bindings for almost all commonly used languages.
source: Most importantly, it includes bindings for almost all commonly used languages.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of the 0MQ library.

claim: Future versions of Heron will address the limitation of not being able to have multiple Nodes on a separate machine interact within that machine by allowing Heron to run Graphs headless.
source: Future versions of Heron will address this limitation by allowing Heron to run Graphs headless (without the GUI process being active), which will allow sub-Graphs to fully run on one machine and communicate their result to Nodes in the machine running Heron.
evidence: Stated as a planned future development.
